title: It Is a Faith Sublime and Sure
description: It Is a Faith Sublime and Sure in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: James Handasyd Perkins wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 356, “Spiritual Presence”. The compilers changed some of the words, and this is their version.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: It is a faith sub-lime and sure, That ev-er round our head Are hov-er-ing, on noise-less wing, The spi-rits of the dead.

lines: It is a faith sublime and sure,
It is a faith sublime and sure,
That it will be our ministry
To bid the mourners cease to mourn,
To bear away from ills of clay

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Handasyd Perkins died in 1849.
credits: Words by James Handasyd Perkins (1810–1849), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
